subject.title: fix(browser): use public ssrf runtime import in CDP proxy bypass

question: Should the browser/Ollama `ssrf-runtime-internal` helpers remain owner-scoped private runtime helpers, or should `registerManagedProxyBrowserCdpBypass` be promoted into the public `ssrf-runtime` SDK contract?
rationale: The current PR is mechanically invalid without making a private managed-proxy CDP bypass helper public or choosing a different private package-resolution path, and that security/API boundary cannot be safely inferred from automation.

options.title: Preserve Owner-Scoped Private Helpers
options.body: Keep the bypass helper out of public `ssrf-runtime` and fix packaged browser/Ollama resolution through the existing private owner-scoped alias or staging path.

options.title: Approve Public SDK Promotion
options.body: Expose the helper through public `ssrf-runtime` only with explicit SDK/security approval, docs, metadata, guardrails, and release-note context.

options.title: Choose A Canonical Sibling Or Replacement
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want one of the sibling candidate PRs or a new maintainer-authored replacement to carry the canonical fix.

recommendation.title: Preserve Owner-Scoped Private Helpers
recommendation.body: Keep the bypass helper out of public `ssrf-runtime` and fix packaged browser/Ollama resolution through the existing private owner-scoped alias or staging path.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans package-boundary hardening, the merged browser helper PR, and the merged private SSRF runtime boundary work that steipete previously merged or authored.
